objective: Five copies of one text normaliser become one. Four test modules carried a private _norm and tests/showcase_parity.py already exported the same function, more completely. #341 asked for the copies to be merged and for the one real question - whether a tag becomes nothing or a space - to be decided explicitly rather than inherited.
completed: Four modules import showcase_parity.norm instead of defining _norm; five copies of the function become one.
The tag question is settled by experiment and the reason is written in showcase_parity.norm's own docstring, where the choice is made.
Each adopting module's docstring says where its normaliser now lives.
All four modules' DECLARED negative controls were re-run and still fire, which is #341's fourth acceptance criterion.
The dual-import idiom of test_showcase_architecture.py is used, so the modules still run both by discovery and by module name from the root; both were exercised.
remaining: Two-axis review of the head commit, then merge.
observations: The shared function already existed and the first survey missed it. WP-109 measured this duplication and reported that a refactor needed a new module; showcase_parity.norm was already there, doing strictly more, and #341's own text pointed at that file as the precedent without noticing it held the function. Looking for the seam before building one would have found it.

The one real question was decided by the suite rather than by preference, which is what made it cheap. Making the module that spaced tags drop them: green. Making the other three space them: test_work_package_loop_page fails, on a page that writes '(Discover 03)' against a record that writes '(Discover 03)'. Its docstring had predicted exactly that case, so the experiment confirmed a comment nobody had tested.

A passing suite would not have been enough here and #341 said so in advance. A refactor of guards can leave every test green while quietly weakening what they catch, so each adopting module's own declared control was re-run as a mutation. All four still fire.

The two modules that keep a private copy were read, not assumed: test_showcase_pages.py neither lowercases nor strips backticks, and test_phase_pages.py normalises a plain label with no markup at all. Merging those would have changed behaviour to no purpose, which is the Speculative Generality the WP-109 measurement declined for designs().
decisions: DEC-112: four copies adopt showcase_parity.norm; a tag becomes nothing, settled by experiment.
assumptions: showcase_parity.norm doing strictly more than the copies it replaces - Markdown links resolved, bold markers stripped - is safe because both sides of every comparison pass through it, and the suite confirms it.

stop_if: A module's private normaliser is replaced without re-running that module's own declared negative control.
test_showcase_pages.py or test_phase_pages.py is made to adopt the shared function; theirs are different by design.

declared_non_coverage: Only _norm is consolidated. designs() keeps its four variants, which differ deliberately - one excludes the security proof, one is keyed by epic - and unifying them needs parameters, as WP-109 measured.
No behaviour of the four modules is otherwise changed, and no page or record is touched.
The controls re-run here are the ones each module declares; a defect a module never claimed to catch is still not caught.
